analysis.title: Galaxy Digital Inc. (GLXY): First Take: Revenue beat driven by digital asset gains; questions on timing of Helios II contract
key_insights: GLXY reported 3Q26 diluted EPS of $0.83 vs GSe $0.54 and Visible Alpha consensus $0.18. Core adj. EPS of $0.74 vs GSe $0.58 and consensus $0.26 (excluding SBC, normalized tax rate).
GS expects a modestly positive reaction given a broad-based revenue beat, trading volumes outperforming industry trends, and Helios I Phase II data center construction on schedule for 2Q27 delivery.

Much of the top-line beat came from larger digital asset gains in Treasury and Corporate, which follow crypto prices. The company has not found a tenant for its ~830MW of approved Helios II capacity, which GS expects to remain an investor focus.

Net revenue was 87% above consensus and 20% above GSe. Treasury and Corporate net revenue was 26% above GSe and Digital assets net revenue was 11% above GSe, with trading volumes up 12% QoQ and AUM up 46% QoQ.

Adj. operating margin was 58.2%, 17.5pp ahead of the Street and in line with GSe. Adj. operating expenses (ex. SBC) were 20% above consensus. Adj. EBITDA of $455mn was 125% above the Street and 26% above GSe.

Global markets net revenue of $53mn rose 8% QoQ and was 18% above GSe on 12% higher volumes QoQ. Management said GLXY volume growth outperformed declining broader spot market volumes, and the average loan book grew 27% QoQ on financing demand.

Asset management net revenue of $19mn rose 11% QoQ, fell 19% YoY and was 4% below GSe. EOP assets under stake of ~$4.6bn rose 64% QoQ and fell 31% YoY. ETF AUM was $2.5bn and Alternatives AUM $3.3bn, up 41% and 30% QoQ, driven by higher digital asset prices and the launch of the Galaxy Sharplink Onchain Yield Fund. Total AUM and AUS rose $3.3bn QoQ to $10.4bn.
Treasury and corporate net revenue of $419mn was 26% above GSe, driven mainly by unrealized gains on digital assets and investment positions. GLXY added to balance sheet digital assets.
Data centers recognized $79mn of net revenue, in line with GSe. Helios I Phase II is on schedule for 2Q27 delivery and the 830MW of Helios II capacity remains uncontracted.

GS looks for clarity on the Helios II expansion outlook, whether higher funding costs across the AI data center ecosystem affect GLXY, what drove Global markets outperformance, and the asset management net flow outlook given modest industry ETF outflows quarter to date.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps a Neutral rating and a $24 12-month target based on a sum-of-the-parts valuation. The target implies 53.1% upside from the $15.68 close on 26 Oct 2026.

crypto_views: GLXY held net BTC exposure of $538mn at 3Q26 vs $400mn at 2Q26, ETH exposure of $128mn vs 0, SOL of $108mn vs $58mn, and net other digital assets of $102mn vs $95mn.
Treasury and Corporate gains were driven mainly by unrealized gains on digital assets, so the revenue beat depends on crypto price trends.
GLXY trading volume growth outperformed broader spot market volume declines.

Upside risks named include favorable crypto regulation, higher crypto market cap and faster institutional uptake of digital assets activity. Downside risks include crypto volatility and persistently lower crypto market cap.
Industry ETF flows are modestly negative quarter to date.
